## The two days

| Day | Topics | Slides |
|-----|--------|--------|
| 1 | Setup and help · packages and environments · NumPy · pandas | [Day 1](day1.html) |
| 2 | Matplotlib · seaborn · SciPy · scikit-image · xarray, dask and napari | [Day 2](day2.html) |

Each day runs **3 hours**, with a 10-minute break. Every block starts with a few minutes of slides, then exercises.

## Before Day 1

1. Install [Miniforge](https://conda-forge.org/download/), which gives you `conda` with conda-forge as the default channel.
2. Get the course materials: `git clone` the course repository, or download it as a ZIP.
3. In a terminal, from the course folder:

```bash
conda env create -f environment.yml
conda activate scientific-python
python check_setup.py
```

Every line should say `OK`. If not, send the output to the instructors **before** Day 1.

**Bring your own laptop:** napari (end of Day 2) opens a desktop window, so it will not work on JupyterHub or a remote server.

## How the exercises work

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
**In the repository**

- `notebooks/`: the exercises
- `solutions/`: worked solutions, released after each block
- `data/`: every dataset we use, so nothing downloads during class
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
**In class**

- Attempt each exercise before looking anything up
- Work with your neighbour
- Put up your hand (or a red sticky note) when stuck
:::
::::

## Where the material comes from

- **Scientific Python Lectures** [@spl]: most NumPy, Matplotlib and SciPy exercises
- **Python Data Science Handbook** [@pdsh]: background reading for NumPy, pandas and plotting
